citations.claim: At first violating step 1 the body has moved under excessive controller force (force 6.5 > fmax 5 per violation).
Initial state was at rest, so the step-1 velocity/energy comes entirely from the controller command on step 1.

counterfactual.change: Set controller noise from 1 to 0; all else identical. Noisy sensor error amplified by kp=100 otherwise pushes commanded force to 6.5 above fmax 5.

explanation: Noisy velocity-error controller exceeds fmax: with kp=100, vcmd=20, fmax=5 and noise=1, the step-1 commanded force is 6.5 > 5. Removing only the noise (1->0) removes the violation, so the noise contribution is added without/after enforcing the fmax clamp (or the clamp is applied before noise).
vision_note: The red controller-driven circle remains on the left side far from the green waypoint in the upper right, showing almost no displacement between step 0 and step 1. No wall contact, tunneling, or escape is visible, so the violation is an invisible excessive commanded force rather than erratic motion.
